messages:
Jamal (Acme): Hey team — embedding endpoint suddenly started returning 400s for our batch job. Worked fine for weeks, now ~30% of requests fail. We're seeing a bunch of "invalid input shape" + some 502 spikes. Anyone seen this?

Alex (Support): Sorry you're hitting this, Jamal. Can you paste the request payload (redact secrets) and the request_id(s) if available? Which model+endpoint are you calling and from which SDK/version?

Jamal (Acme): Thanks. We're calling POST /v1/embeddings model: text-embedding-1536. SDK is our in-house wrapper over the REST API (not official Redwood SDK). Example payload that failed: 
```json
{
  "input": [0.021, -0.13, 0.55, ... 1536 numbers total ...]
}
```
The error response: 
```json
{
  "error": "invalid_input_shape",
  "message": "expected array of vectors: got vector of length 1536; endpoint expects [n,1536]"
}
```
We have some clients that call single-text -> single-vector, others call list-of-text -> list-of-vectors. I thought the API accepted both but maybe SDK broke. Also seeing requests where payload was `[[[0.1,0.2...]]]` (extra nesting from our batching).

Alex (Support): That error is helpful. Two quick questions: 1) When you say 502 spikes, are those correlated with the weirdly-nested payloads? 2) Any chance your wrapper sometimes double-wraps lists (e.g., wraps an already-list into another list) during its batching step?

Jamal (Acme): 1) yes, the 502s line up with the high payload-size requests. 2) We think so — our batching code does `if isinstance(item, list): batch.append(item)` and elsewhere `batch = [batch]` in a hurry. Oops. Repro attached.

Maria (Eng): @Alex can you forward the request_id for one failing request? I'll grep serving logs. Also, can Jamal share the exact curl they used (or the raw HTTP body). If the wrapper is creating nested arrays we might be hitting an unexpected code path that tries to coerce shapes and then blows memory.

Jamal (Acme): One failing request id: req_1801234608. Raw body (trimmed): 
```http
POST /v1/embeddings HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "input": [[0.02, -0.11, ... 1536 numbers ...]]
}
```
Also we reproduced locally: sometimes there is one extra nesting level (`[[[...]]]`).

InfraBot: detected request req_1801234608: payload_size=1.2MB, shape_guess=[[1536]] -> normalized_shape_attempt=[1,1536], kernel_allocation=large, GC spike, backend-500s observed on serving-host-7

Priya (SRE): Thanks infra bot. That aligns with our trace: host-7 saw OOMs around the same window. The runtime tried to batch the request with others assuming shape [n,1536], but when later coalescing it saw mismatched ranks and did defensive copies -> huge mem blow.

Maria (Eng): Repro plan: Jamal, can you run two quick experiments for us?
1) Send a single request with "input": [0.02, -0.11, ...] (flat vector) and include header X-Debug: true to get server-shape-info.
2) Send a request with "input": [[0.02, -0.11, ...]] (list-of-vectors) and one with "input": [[[...]]] (extra nest). Capture responses.
Also include the exact Content-Type header and any encoding (we've seen clients send application/json but with `input` serialized as a string).

Jamal (Acme): Ran them. Results:
- Flat vector ("input": [0.02,...]) -> 400 invalid_input_shape message (server expects top-level array-of-vectors).
- Single-nested ([[...]]) -> 200, embedding returned (as expected).
- Double-nested ([[[...]]]) -> 400 + occasionally 502 on server; payload size looks bigger because some internal path mistakenly serializes as JSON string before parsing.
Response bodies:
```json
{ "error": "invalid_input_shape", "expected": "[n,1536] or [n,string]", "received_shape": "[1] (nested depth 3)" }
```

Alex (Support): So root cause seems to be client-side: some callers send flat vectors instead of wrapping them as a single-item list, and some callers over-wrap causing nested arrays. Both create server-side error paths (and the over-wrapping can trigger memory blow when the runtime attempts to normalize shapes).

Maria (Eng): Agreed. Action items:
- Immediate: Alex to share guidance + a small validation snippet Jamal can add to their wrapper to normalize inputs (wrap scalars/flat vector into list, flatten accidental extra nesting to one level). Also advise to upgrade to official SDK until we ship server-side guards.
- Short term: Eng to add stricter validation on the API surface with clear errors (e.g., "expected top-level array of vectors or strings; got nested array depth 3") — ticket ENG-4512.
- SRE: Add runtime defensive limits to reject >2 nested levels cheaply to avoid memory blow; alert on large payload_size on serving hosts.

Priya (SRE): I'll add a temporary mitigation: reject requests with content-length > 512KB to return 413 until validation lands (careful: could impact legitimate large batches). Will throttle by IP for now to reduce blast radius.

Alex (Support): Jamal, here are two small helpers you can drop into your wrapper today:
```python
# normalize_input.py
def normalize_embedding_input(x):
    # Accept: flat vector, list of vectors, or list of strings.
    # Ensure top-level is a list of vectors or strings, no deeper than 1 nesting.
    while isinstance(x, list) and len(x)==1 and isinstance(x[0], list):
        x = x[0]  # unwrap accidental double-wrapping
    if not x or (isinstance(x, list) and (isinstance(x[0], (int,float)) or isinstance(x[0], list))):
        # if a single flat vector -> wrap as list\        if isinstance(x[0], (int,float)):
            return [x]
    return x
```
Also instrument the wrapper to log len(json.dumps(payload)) before send so you can catch big ones.

Jamal (Acme): Thanks, Alex. We'll patch normalization today and roll a fix to our batching. Can you also confirm if you'll issue a partial credit for the billing spike? We had many client retries.

Alex (Support): I'll open a credit request for the impacted window and send to billing. We'll need the invoice window + list of request_ids (you already shared req_1801234608; any others please paste).

Maria (Eng): From the engineering side, we'll prioritize ENG-4512 to provide clearer 4xx for nested-depth and add a cheap pre-parse size check so those requests fail fast instead of hitting the heavy code path. ETA: 2 days for a patch, 1 week for rollout.

Priya (SRE): I'll also add an alert to notify us when the serving host memory pressure is above 70% and the recent requests include content-length > 512KB. That should help catch regressions.

Jamal (Acme): Patch deployed. After normalization, errors dropped to 0 and throughput stable. Appreciate the fast triage and credit help.

Alex (Support): Glad that helped. We'll follow up once ENG-4512 lands and when billing confirms credits. If you notice anything else, ping this thread or DM.
